actions: Check engine oil level and correct viscosity/spec first.
If it’s cold-start only and fades within 30–90 seconds, monitor for a few days and avoid hard revs while cold.
If it persists longer than about 2 minutes or worsens, verify oil pressure and inspect for restriction such as filter or oil galley blockage.
stop_now_if: Oil pressure warning light appears or the tick becomes suddenly loud with power loss.
Noise becomes constant even when fully warm.
ignore_risk: Can progress to accelerated valvetrain wear and rough running.

actions: Confirm pattern: brief 1–3 second rattle on cold start then gone is classic tensioner behavior.
Reduce repeated short start/stop cycles temporarily because they repeat the same chain slap.
If the rattle gets longer or louder, inspect tensioner and guides before timing jumps.
stop_now_if: Rattle becomes sustained or appears with misfire, rough running, or check engine light.
Harsh rattle under acceleration that instantly quiets on lift-off.
ignore_risk: Chain slack can worsen and potentially jump timing, causing major internal damage.

actions: Track whether it’s only cold and disappears quickly when warm.
Use correct oil spec and a quality filter because oil pressure stability matters.
If it evolves, inspect tensioner, guides, and oil control path.
stop_now_if: Noise starts lasting longer or appears when warm.
ignore_risk: May slowly progress into guide wear and severe timing noise.

actions: Test: is it loudest on decel or lift-off or during load transitions? That fits guide wear.
Avoid high RPM and hard kickdown until inspected.
Inspect guides and tensioner promptly.
stop_now_if: Rattle becomes violent with power loss, misfire, or check engine light.
ignore_risk: High risk of timing jump and valve/piston damage depending on engine design.

actions: Test: if it appears under load and quiets immediately when you lift, consider phaser control and knock separation.
Verify oil level and oil quality because VVT is oil-pressure dependent.
If timing-related codes exist, inspect VVT solenoid and phaser operation.
stop_now_if: Strong vibration or roughness appears with metallic noise under load.
ignore_risk: Can worsen into persistent timing noise and poor performance.

actions: If symptoms started after an oil service, confirm correct oil spec and level.
Pull trouble codes if a light is on because this is a shortcut to the real cause.
Inspect VVT solenoids and oil control path and verify actual cam timing.
stop_now_if: Severe misfire or limp mode behavior appears under throttle.
ignore_risk: Ongoing timing instability increases stress, fuel use, and drivability issues.

actions: Confirm it’s a light, even tick that cleanly follows RPM with no performance symptoms.
Listen near injectors because direct-injection engines often tick normally.
If misfire or roughness appears, shift to ignition or fuel diagnosis.
ignore_risk: Usually harmless when no other symptoms exist.

actions: Localize the noise: top of engine versus front accessory drive.
In Park or Neutral, hold 1500 RPM. If it tracks RPM, it is valvetrain or accessory related.
If it gets harsher or louder, inspect rocker, lifter, or valve lash path.
stop_now_if: Harsh mechanical tap appears with power loss or strong shake.
ignore_risk: Can progress into mechanical wear and misfire if severe.

actions: Track heat relation: if it fades warm, it is often minor.
Confirm correct oil spec and filter quality.
If it grows over time, inspect valvetrain components.
stop_now_if: Tick becomes loud with clear misfire or rough running.
ignore_risk: Often low risk, but long neglect can accelerate wear.

actions: Do not continue driving if it’s grinding or hammering. Treat it as urgent mechanical contact risk.
Check oil level immediately.
Tow for inspection because valvetrain or internal contact is possible.
stop_now_if: Any sustained grinding or hammering noise.
ignore_risk: Rapid internal engine damage.

actions: Cold start: a sharp tick near the manifold that changes as it warms fits a small leak.
Look for soot marks around manifold or joints.
Repair gasket or fasteners before it spreads.
ignore_risk: Usually a noise and efficiency issue. It can worsen and affect sensors over time.

actions: Warm-only tick suggests a crack or joint opening with thermal expansion.
Inspect for soot at cracks and joints.
Repair before the crack grows.
ignore_risk: Can expand into a larger leak and drivability or sensor issues.

actions: If it’s louder on acceleration and quieter on coast, an exhaust pressure leak is likely.
Inspect manifold, downpipe joints, and flex section.
Repair to prevent expansion.
ignore_risk: Leak may grow and become louder and can affect mixture readings.

actions: With engine cool, lightly press or tap the shield area to reproduce the buzz.
Replace missing clips or fasteners.
Ensure no contact with the exhaust.
ignore_risk: Mostly nuisance, but it can worsen and vibrate into contact.

actions: If it rattles on bumps or load changes, inspect hangers and rubber mounts.
Confirm the exhaust isn’t hitting the body or subframe.
Replace worn hangers or mounts.
stop_now_if: Exhaust is dragging or striking the body hard.
ignore_risk: Can crack pipes or welds and create leaks.

actions: Hold RPM at the noise range while parked. If it happens, it is exhaust or body resonance.
Inspect muffler or resonator for internal baffle failure.
Replace the resonator or muffler if confirmed.
ignore_risk: Usually noise only. Severe internal collapse can restrict flow in rare cases.

actions: If it appears only with speed or wind, inspect undertray and fasteners immediately.
Secure loose edges so they can’t flap into tires.
Replace missing clips or screws.
stop_now_if: Panel is hanging low or contacting tires.
ignore_risk: Can detach and cause damage or a driving hazard.

actions: Do not keep driving because this is metal-to-rotor grinding.
Avoid repeated braking and let the brakes cool.
Replace pads immediately and likely rotors and inspect caliper condition.
stop_now_if: Any grinding during braking.
ignore_risk: Rotor destruction, caliper damage, and dangerous braking loss.

actions: Perform a gentle lane-change test: if noise changes with load shift, bearing is likely.
After a short drive, carefully compare hub temperature side to side.
Plan bearing replacement before it progresses.
stop_now_if: Hum becomes grinding, strong vibration appears, or wheel feels loose.
ignore_risk: Can progress to failure and loss of control risk.

actions: Stop safely immediately.
Check lug nut tightness with the proper tool.
If you can’t verify tightness, tow the vehicle.
stop_now_if: Any suspicion of wheel looseness.
ignore_risk: Wheel can detach.

actions: If squeal lasts a few seconds on cold start, inspect belt and tensioner condition.
Increase electrical load, such as lights or defrost. If squeal worsens, slip is likely.
Replace belt and or tensioner as needed.
stop_now_if: Battery light or overheat warning appears or steering assist suddenly changes if belt-driven.
ignore_risk: Belt can fail and take down charging, cooling, or assist systems depending on vehicle.

actions: Add electrical load. If the whine changes, alternator involvement increases.
Watch for charging warnings or voltage instability.
Inspect or replace alternator before failure.
stop_now_if: Grinding with battery warning or severe electrical instability.
ignore_risk: Charging failure can strand the vehicle.

actions: Toggle A/C. If the noise changes, compressor or clutch path is likely.
If grinding begins, avoid using A/C to reduce load until inspected.
Inspect compressor bearing or clutch before it seizes and throws the belt.
stop_now_if: Strong grinding or belt distress noises.
ignore_risk: Compressor seizure can damage the belt drive and cause loss of systems.

actions: If there is a hiss at idle with rough or lean symptoms, suspect unmetered air leak.
Inspect vacuum hoses, PCV lines, and intake ducting.
If lean codes exist, fix leaks first before chasing sensors.
ignore_risk: Lean running can overheat combustion and worsen drivability.

actions: At idle, press the brake pedal. If RPM changes and hiss increases, booster leak is likely.
If brake feel changes, such as hard pedal or weak assist, treat as urgent.
Inspect booster and check valve immediately.
stop_now_if: Brake assist becomes weak or pedal becomes abnormally hard.
ignore_risk: Direct braking safety risk.

actions: Reduce throttle immediately. Do not load the engine while pinging.
If available, test one tank of higher octane only as a diagnostic hint, not a permanent fix.
Investigate root causes: heat, lean condition, ignition, VVT, or carbon buildup.
stop_now_if: Knock becomes harsh with power loss even at light throttle.
ignore_risk: Severe knock can damage pistons or valves over time, rapidly if intense.

actions: Do not drive. Deep knock under load suggests bottom-end damage risk.
Check oil level immediately.
Tow for oil pressure verification and bearing inspection.
stop_now_if: Any deep knock that worsens with throttle.
ignore_risk: Catastrophic engine failure such as a thrown rod is possible.

actions: If it’s cold-only and disappears warm, keep revs low until warmed up.
Avoid hard acceleration when cold.
If it starts occurring when warm, reassess diagnosis.
ignore_risk: Often moderate, but persistent warm knock needs re-evaluation.

actions: Do the two isolation checks: rev in Park or Neutral for RPM relation and steady-speed test for speed relation.
Report whether it is cold-only or warm-only.
Report whether it is worse under load or on coast.
ignore_risk: Without relation data, multiple causes overlap and diagnosis becomes guesswork.

actions: Record 10 seconds at idle and 10 seconds at about 1500 RPM near the source.
Confirm whether it follows RPM while parked or only road speed.
Confirm whether it is cold-only, warm-only, or both.
ignore_risk: Overlapping causes without relation tests.

actions: Engine test: does the same sound appear while stationary when you raise RPM?
Wheel test: does the sound change during a gentle lane shift at the same speed?
Once separated, the diagnosis becomes high-confidence.
ignore_risk: Wrong path wastes time and can miss safety issues.
